item.title: Translatome data of bundle sheath and mesophyll cells of leaves of the C4 species Flaveria bidentis
item.description:
Stefanie Schulze, Peter Westhoff
Scientific Data, vol. 13, issue 1
DOI: 10.1038/s41597-026-08636-8
Abstract C 4 photosynthesis, a specialized form of photosynthesis that uses a CO 2 concentrating mechanism, evolved more than 60 times independently within various families of the angiosperms. This evolution entailed anatomical and biochemical changes within the plants which were accompanied by a plethora of differentially expressed genes. The differentiation of bundle sheath and mesophyll cells in the leaves was an essential anatomical adaption in many C 4 species and was accompanied by a differential distribution of photosynthetic processes between these two cell types, whereas in C 3 species each leaf chlorenchyma cell is able of carrying out all photosynthetic reactions. Leaves of the C 4 Asteracean species Flaveria bidentis were used to generate translatome data for bundle sheath and mesophyll cells allowing to elucidate which genes are expressed differentially between these cell types.
